To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a simple and powerful principle exists for defining fairness in systems with multiple resources, and that a packet-by-packet fair algorithm can be constructed based on this principle for the joint allocation processing and bandwidth resources.

(i) the problem of achieving fairness when the bandwidth and processor resources are jointly allocated can be reduced to the problem of achieving max-min fairness in the allocation bandwidth and processor resources; (ii) the joint allocation of bandwidth and processor resources can be achieved using a simple packet-by-packet scheduling algorithm that uses a single counter per flow and that is fair, stable and scalable.

a) we propose a general principle to define fairness in systems with multiple resources, and b) we propose a practical packet-by-packet joint bandwidth and processing resource allocation algorithm which is provably fair.

the problem of defining fairness in systems with multiple resources and with the development of practical algorithms for the joint allocation that achieve such fairness.
the problem of achieving fairness when two resources (such as bandwidth and processing) are jointly allocated.
achieving fairness in the sharing of multiple resources, which is an important problem in many areas of computer science and engineering.
